title: Pericentric inversion of chromosome 9
clinical_history: Demonstration metaphase prepared for laboratory teaching. One chromosome 9 has a pericentric inversion of the heterochromatin region. No clinical abnormality is provided.
unknown_prompt: The chromosome count is 46 and the arms of chromosome 9 are still both present. Compare the band order of the two chromosomes 9, then write the karyotype. Do not assign a disease from this finding alone.
plain_language_interpretation: A male karyotype with 46 chromosomes and a pericentric inversion of one chromosome 9, with breakpoints at p12 and q13. The chromosome length is unchanged because the segment is reversed.
diagnosis: No disease is assigned from this karyotype alone
diagnosis_options: No disease is assigned from this karyotype alone
explanation: A pericentric inversion reverses a segment that includes the centromere. inv(9)(p12q13) is a common heteromorphic change. The two chromosomes 9 stay the same length; the band order between p12 and q13 is reversed on one homolog. This teaching case does not assign a syndrome from that finding.
hints: Count the chromosomes first. An inversion does not change the count.
Compare the two chromosomes 9. Look for a reversed band order around the centromere, not a missing arm.
Write the breakpoints inside one set of parentheses with no semicolon: inv(9)(p12q13).
